demands.belongsTo: Beckett’s plays (Waiting for Godot’s cross-talk and clown business)

briefs.title: Proof Of Arrival
briefs.objective: Get her name on the register before the window closes at five.
briefs.obstacle: Each rule the clerk explains needs the thing the last rule forbids, and he means every word kindly.

briefs.title: The Answer On Page Four
briefs.objective: Say one thing, any one thing, that isn’t typed in the folder.
briefs.obstacle: Whatever he tries turns up on the next page, and the interviewer is only ever pleased to find it there.

briefs.title: The Loading Bay
briefs.objective: Get the keys back before the shutter reaches the floor.
briefs.obstacle: He is bigger, he has the keys, and every second she spends talking the shutter drops another foot.

briefs.title: The Safe Behind The Ring
briefs.objective: Make him drop the pry bar and go down the front stairs with his pockets empty.
briefs.obstacle: He’s younger and faster, he knows which shoulder is the bad one, and he fears the men he owes more than he fears her.

briefs.title: Second Tier
briefs.objective: Get the ring box back and the cake out on time, without a sound reaching the speeches.
briefs.obstacle: He’s quicker than she is, the cake is between them, and every crash she makes could be heard through the door.

briefs.title: Her First Day On The Detail
briefs.objective: Get him from the service elevator to the van at the dock in four minutes, unphotographed and in one piece.
briefs.obstacle: He stops for every camera angle, reads his followers’ comments aloud, asks her to do things again for the stream, and the photographer is somewhere between them and the dock.

briefs.title: The Last Well
briefs.objective: Get water and go on with the route still in her hands.
briefs.obstacle: He holds the rope, he knows the desert better than she does, and the sun is coming up.

briefs.title: Her Mother’s Ice Axe
briefs.objective: Get out the door and up the last ridge while the summit is still clear.
briefs.obstacle: He’s right about the weather, he won’t argue, and he’s standing in the only doorway.

briefs.title: The Receiver
briefs.objective: Close the file without ruining him and without risking her own post.
briefs.obstacle: The rules are clear, the patrol has already logged it, and the boy keeps asking her if she has ever heard what’s out there.

briefs.title: Column Nine
briefs.objective: Get the corrected column worked, checked and out to the radio stations by six, without the hall losing its nerve.
briefs.obstacle: Ninety minutes is barely enough to work the column once, the hall has been at it since dawn, and every person down there will hear in her voice how wrong the warning would have been.

briefs.title: High Wind
briefs.objective: Make her let go of the string.
briefs.obstacle: She loves him, she’s stubborn, and he can only reach her with his voice over the wind.

briefs.title: The Puddle On Larch Street
briefs.objective: As Lefty, get both boots into the puddle before Juniper gives up and walks around it; as Righty, keep them dry.
briefs.obstacle: The same voice has to win and lose the argument, and the two boots have to sound like two people the animators can draw.

briefs.title: Last Launch From The Roof
briefs.objective: Say goodbye without letting him see it matters.
briefs.obstacle: He won’t accept it, and every line has to fit a mouth that opens and closes on the picture’s timing, not hers.

briefs.title: The Spillway Walk
briefs.objective: Keep him walking and keep him calm until he reaches the far side.
briefs.obstacle: The wheel is slipping, he freezes whenever he looks down, and every word has to land on drawings that won’t wait for her.

briefs.title: Seat Fourteen
briefs.objective: Find out if she was all right, without telling her who he is.
briefs.obstacle: She’s a stranger to him now, the bus is only twelve stops, and if he names himself she might get off.

briefs.title: The Last Thing Handed In
briefs.objective: Open and close the last story in the voice she has used for every other one.
briefs.obstacle: The glove is hers, the rhymes written for her say so plainly, and her voice wants to change.

briefs.title: The Seed Corn
briefs.objective: Keep the seed for planting and keep Cal on her side.
briefs.obstacle: He’s right that his children are hungry now, and she owes him.

briefs.title: One More School Night
briefs.objective: Give him one more ordinary school night, and keep her promise never to lie to him.
briefs.obstacle: He has seen the soldiers, he’s waiting for her to say it, and she isn’t allowed to until eight tomorrow.

demands.belongsTo: Modernist / auteur art cinema (Bresson, Antonioni) and the slow-cinema strand; director-specific methods

briefs.title: Oranges
briefs.objective: Let him finish without giving him the argument he’s braced for.
briefs.obstacle: He keeps leaving silences for her to fill, and the house is the only thing she has left of the last six years.

briefs.title: Three Replies
briefs.objective: Leave him a reply she can bear to send.
briefs.obstacle: Every reply she starts turns into the argument they had nine years ago, and the phone keeps whichever one she doesn’t delete.

briefs.title: Instructions For Leaving A Room
briefs.objective: Carry out every instruction completely, each time it comes.
briefs.obstacle: The instructions never change, and the performer does: by the third time, putting on the coat means something it didn’t the first.

briefs.title: A Score Without Words
briefs.objective: Turn every mark on the four pages into sound, in order, without words.
briefs.obstacle: The score has no key, the marks mean whatever the voice makes them mean, and the last page is empty.

briefs.title: Places For The Finale
briefs.objective: Get the number right before the cue light goes green.
briefs.obstacle: She keeps forgetting the second verse, the time step at the bridge keeps tripping her, and the band is already playing the intro.

briefs.title: The Song For Act Two
briefs.objective: Sell him the number tonight, sung and danced herself, so the second act has its opener by morning.
briefs.obstacle: He gives her almost nothing to play off, the song is three hours old, and she writes songs for dancers without being one.

demands.belongsTo: productions that ask actors to ride, as The Wild Angels did

briefs.title: No Patch Tonight
briefs.objective: Send him back to his mother’s farm before the life gets him.
briefs.obstacle: He has nothing else he wants, he has done everything they asked, and she can’t tell him the real reason for the vote.

briefs.title: The Founder’s Bike
briefs.objective: Leave with the title signed over to her so she can sell it.
briefs.obstacle: Her father wrote the rule himself, Walt has kept that engine running for thirty years, and he’s the last person alive who still treats her like family.

briefs.title: The Last Broadcast
briefs.objective: Get through the sign-off as herself, with nothing for the new owners to cut.
briefs.obstacle: She hasn’t written a farewell, Otto is crying in the booth, and the people listening have been with her for twenty years.

briefs.title: The Defense In Room Twelve
briefs.objective: Defend the thesis so completely that the faculty can’t vote it down, without giving him the outburst he’s trying to provoke.
briefs.obstacle: He has found a real gap in her second proof, the room is on his side, and her documented habit means her anger can only show as slowness.

briefs.title: The Wrong Urn
briefs.objective: Make him tell her where her husband actually is.
briefs.obstacle: There’s nowhere to tell her: he’s in the sea, and the manager keeps offering forms and percentages.

briefs.title: Not To Be Admitted
briefs.objective: Get an order of service down that the funeral home will actually use, while her mother still has the strength to dictate.
briefs.obstacle: Her mother keeps adding names, wants every reason read out in full at the door, and laughs herself into coughing fits.

briefs.title: Sundown On Calloway Street
briefs.objective: Get him and his trade off the block by sundown, with the block behind her and no gun in it.
briefs.obstacle: He has men behind him, money in the neighborhood and no reason to be afraid of one nurse.

briefs.title: The Garland Avenue Ledger
briefs.objective: Get his signed statement naming the landlord by five o’clock.
briefs.obstacle: He has the department, the city attorney and the landlord’s money behind him, and he thinks a Black woman with a photocopy is a problem he can wait out.

demands.belongsTo: practical-effects roles in heavy prosthetics

briefs.title: The Left Hand
briefs.objective: Make him believe her and take the hand seriously before tonight.
briefs.obstacle: The scans are clean, she sounds unwell, and the hand behaves while he’s looking at it.

briefs.title: What Grows Under The Bandage
briefs.objective: Make him see it the way she does before he calls anyone.
briefs.obstacle: What’s under the bandage is horrifying, he wants to drive her to the hospital tonight, and part of her knows he’s right.

briefs.title: Three States For A Cake
briefs.objective: Get back on the road with the route he planned.
briefs.obstacle: She has bought a map at the counter and won’t get back in the car unless she drives.

briefs.title: The Tent At Site Forty
briefs.objective: Get the tent up and both of them inside before the rain the forecast promised.
briefs.obstacle: The poles don’t match the diagram, Benny reads the steps out of order, and the more carefully Martin plans the worse it gets.

briefs.title: Stakeout On Pell Avenue
briefs.objective: Get through the night without telling him why she transferred.
briefs.obstacle: He’s a good detective, and he has worked it out already.

briefs.title: Undercover At The Copper Lamp
briefs.objective: Stay in cover until the forger makes his sale, then signal her partner without the room noticing.
briefs.obstacle: She can’t sing, she can’t stop singing, and her partner keeps talking in her ear about everything except what she needs.

briefs.title: Forty Seconds In Gallery Nine
briefs.objective: Leave the gallery with something worth the night before the patrol turns the corner.
briefs.obstacle: The prize is a fake, her plan has nothing after this point, and he has an idea she didn’t think of.

briefs.title: One Signature Short
briefs.objective: Get her to agree to forge one signature by Friday.
briefs.obstacle: She retired for good, she made a promise to her granddaughter, and she’s enjoying watching him try.

briefs.title: The Checkpoint At Usui
briefs.objective: Get through the barrier with the letter, without killing his student.
briefs.obstacle: The student can’t let him pass without losing his post and his honor, and the student is the faster swordsman now.

briefs.title: Eleven Forms For The Scroll
briefs.objective: Get every form onto the scroll exactly as it’s done, before the light goes.
briefs.obstacle: A brush can catch only stillness and the forms are motion, his knees won’t hold the low guards for long, and the eleventh was never meant for anyone but an heir.

briefs.title: Through The Back
briefs.objective: Get through the back door before the man reaches the window.
briefs.obstacle: The attendant doesn’t know her, the rule is the rule, and she has no breath to explain with.

briefs.title: Ahead Of The Sweep Bus
briefs.objective: Cross the line before the bus passes her, at her own pace.
briefs.obstacle: The bus is gaining, her hip has been bad since the eleventh mile, and her grandson keeps pushing her to run when running is what hurts.

briefs.title: The Greenhouse Window
briefs.objective: Get through the whole apology without being interrupted.
briefs.obstacle: She isn’t angry at all, and that throws him completely.

briefs.title: Two Names On The Ballot
briefs.objective: Keep her best friend, whoever wins the vote.
briefs.obstacle: Her friend wants to win too, her friend’s speech is funnier, and Maya’s first feeling is that she wants her to lose.

briefs.title: The Christmas Eve Loaf
briefs.objective: Hand over the loaf and get back on the road before she feels anything.
briefs.obstacle: He tells her his wife died in the summer, and he ordered it anyway.

briefs.title: The Box With His Name On It
briefs.objective: Get him to open the present before her own children come back and the moment goes.
briefs.obstacle: Every present he has been given went back in a bag at the next move, so he’d rather not want this one, and she can’t promise him he’ll stay.

rows.label: Comedy
playsOfKind: The Playboy Of The Western World

briefs.title: The Best Man’s Draft
briefs.objective: Get one laugh out of her before the bar closes.
briefs.obstacle: Every story in the speech is wrong in some detail she knows, and she says so.

briefs.title: Out The Door By Seven
briefs.objective: Leave the house by seven, sure the twins will be fine without him.
briefs.obstacle: Every instruction reminds him of two more, she seems far too relaxed about all of them, and each “last thing” costs a minute his wife is counting.

briefs.title: Last Week’s Pay
briefs.objective: Get the money he’s owed and leave still thinking well of her.
briefs.obstacle: She has the money for her car payment and none for him, and every excuse she gives makes her smaller in his eyes.

briefs.title: Saturday At Ten
briefs.objective: Quit the lessons today, out loud, and still have him on her side when she walks out.
briefs.obstacle: He already paid for the entry out of his own pocket, he answers with silences she can’t read, and half of her wants him to talk her out of it.

demands.belongsTo: Concert films of singers and vocal acts (the singing performers themselves)

briefs.title: The Count-In
briefs.objective: Get him to sing the song for the children before the count runs out.
briefs.obstacle: The drummer is already clicking the count, every word has to go off-mic and through a smile for the pit cameras, and Nico has told her twice he’ll never play it in front of people.

briefs.title: Hold The Room
briefs.objective: Keep the crowd with her until the guitar is back, and make the gap the part of the set people remember.
briefs.obstacle: His estimates keep changing, every minute she fills comes out of her set, and the one song she wrote to be sung with no guitar is the one she swore she’d never sing at a festival.

briefs.title: The Amended Minutes
briefs.objective: Find out whether he altered the minutes, and who asked him to.
briefs.obstacle: If she asks straight out and he did it, he’ll know about her copy, and she has no idea who he’d tell.

briefs.title: The Revised Forecast
briefs.objective: Get his say-so to put the flood warning back into tonight’s forecast before the countdown ends.
briefs.obstacle: He says the paragraph came from upstairs and it’s routine, the countdown won’t stop, and if she reads the warning without his say, she’s off the air tonight.

briefs.title: The Same Depth
briefs.objective: Get him to cancel tomorrow’s survey without telling him what she thinks the number means.
briefs.obstacle: The data is clean and the instruments check out, and the calmer she stays, the more he thinks she’s unwell.

briefs.title: The Eleventh Count
briefs.objective: Leave a record plain enough that the relief team counts the stars before they decide she was ill.
briefs.obstacle: The count sounds impossible, she can’t know whether anyone else has seen it, the log is an official document, and the longer she talks the closer she comes to saying what she believes it means.

briefs.title: Quarter Day
briefs.objective: Leave with her wages in hand and her good character intact.
briefs.obstacle: The custom of the house forbids her to sit until invited, or to name a sum first, and Mrs. Ashworth knows it and offers a glowing reference in place of the money.

briefs.title: The Second Fitting
briefs.objective: Let Clara know she has guessed, and that the gown will keep the secret, without saying a word that could be repeated.
briefs.obstacle: A dressmaker known to have hidden such a thing would lose every customer in the county, the girl’s mother pays the bills and will inspect every seam at four, and Clara is too frightened to say anything but how happy she is.

briefs.title: Redirect
briefs.objective: Let the jury hear, in the grandmother’s own words, that her grandson was home when she said he was.
briefs.obstacle: She can’t put the answers in the witness’s mouth, and after the cross Mrs. Lyle is afraid of every question.

briefs.title: Before Sentence Is Passed
briefs.objective: Get the judge to hear a plea for a shorter sentence from the one person in the room with the right to make it.
briefs.obstacle: A victim statement is meant to describe the harm, the judge can stop her when she strays from it, and her parents are behind her, hearing it for the first time.

demands.belongsTo: the creature performer role in practical-effects (suit or prosthetic) creature films

briefs.title: The Boat Shed
briefs.objective: Keep the shed closed and get him off the dock before the tide turns.
briefs.obstacle: He’s responsible for the boats inside, he thinks she’s overreacting, and something in the shed has gone quiet.

briefs.title: The Dispensary Door
briefs.objective: Keep him still and quiet until she has the dose drawn and a plan to use it.
briefs.obstacle: He’s panicking, he’s sure he can reach the truck, and every time he raises his voice the thing on the other side of the door goes quiet and listens.

briefs.title: Friday’s Count
briefs.objective: Get the money back by Friday and keep him alive.
briefs.obstacle: He’s spent it, he thinks she’s threatening him, and she can’t tell him what her brother does to people who steal without saying it out loud in the office.

briefs.title: Tuesday Night, All Night
briefs.objective: Find out what he did that night before she agrees to anything.
briefs.obstacle: The more he tells her, the more she’s part of it, he keeps bringing their son into it, and she still can’t tell when he’s lying.

demands.belongsTo: Action-led cyberpunk in the mould of The Matrix (martial-arts and wirework set pieces), not the genre as a whole

briefs.title: Reclamation Window
briefs.objective: Keep her hearing for one more week, until her new job starts.
briefs.obstacle: The clerk has no authority to extend anything, and the script he reads from has an answer for every argument she makes.

briefs.title: The Summer He Sold
briefs.objective: Make him buy the summer back before midnight.
briefs.obstacle: He can’t afford it, he doesn’t remember what he sold, and to him she’s asking him to pay for a stranger’s memories.

briefs.title: The Phrase
briefs.objective: Give Hana the phrase as it was meant to be danced, so it outlives her in the company.
briefs.obstacle: Her knee won’t take many more runs, and as she dances she can see Hana is already better at it than she wants to admit.

briefs.title: The Box Step
briefs.objective: Learn the waltz well enough to dance it at the wedding the way she would have wanted.
briefs.obstacle: He has two left feet and no partner to dance with, the old man is a demanding teacher, and every count reminds both of them who should be here.

demands.belongsTo: creature roles in prosthetics

briefs.title: The Well Tithe
briefs.objective: Make the bargain without her daughter’s name in it.
briefs.obstacle: It knows the name already, it enjoys the bargaining, and the old form of the bargain doesn’t let her lie.

briefs.title: What The Mirror Keeps
briefs.objective: Get her out of the house before the lady wakes, without telling her what’s in the glass.
briefs.obstacle: She thinks a talking mirror is a trick worth more money, the mirror can use only voices that belonged to others, and the lady’s voice keeps breaking through.

briefs.title: Three Cups
briefs.objective: Get her to say who the third cup belonged to.
briefs.obstacle: She’s protecting her son, who visited that evening, and every answer she gives is polite and true and leaves him out.

briefs.title: Seven Minutes Fast
briefs.objective: Get him to release the farmhand and look again at the brother-in-law.
briefs.obstacle: He has made his arrest and the press is waiting, the brother-in-law is a churchwarden, and her only evidence is a confession that she tampered with the town clock.

demands.belongsTo: productions that shoot their peril practically

briefs.title: Floor Eleven
briefs.objective: Keep him awake and calm until the crew arrives.
briefs.obstacle: He’s going into shock, every aftershock frightens them both, and she has no idea whether the floor will hold.

briefs.title: Still On The Air
briefs.objective: Get her listeners, and Mr. Petrakis above all, to the shelters before the storm surge.
briefs.obstacle: She can’t see what’s happening outside, the generator is running down, and Mr. Petrakis says he’s ridden out worse and won’t leave his late wife’s garden.

briefs.title: The Inquiry Room
briefs.objective: Get on the record that she warned the mill office at nine, three hours before the dam failed.
briefs.obstacle: Counsel wants yes and no, her statement was taken badly in 1962, and her own memory goes in and out with the details.

briefs.title: At The Ministry Door
briefs.objective: Get the petition into the minister’s hands today.
briefs.obstacle: The doorkeeper has his orders and a family to keep, the minister won’t come down, and she has been on her feet so long that standing still is harder than walking.

briefs.title: Closing Day
briefs.objective: Get through the last sale without making it a goodbye.
briefs.obstacle: He wants it to be one, and he’s brought something with him.

briefs.title: The Claim Ticket
briefs.objective: Find the rabbit, or send him away kindly, before the counter shuts.
briefs.obstacle: He has no claim ticket, he can only half describe it, and the rules say no item leaves without one.

briefs.title: Letters From The Lock
briefs.objective: Read the letters so the audience hears a woman writing to her sister, and only then a documentary’s narration.
briefs.obstacle: There’s no picture of her and no one to play off, the footage dictates the timing, and the letters have to age twelve years in three minutes.

briefs.title: Scratch Narration
briefs.objective: Record a narration he’ll let her keep, before the lock in the morning.
briefs.obstacle: He objects to every word that makes him sound important, the cut leaves her no room for more words, and the line he hates most is the one she thinks is true.

briefs.title: The Thermostat
briefs.objective: Get him to admit they never really decided about his mother.
briefs.obstacle: He keeps it about the thermostat, and she’s tired and doesn’t want to be the one who says she doesn’t want his mother there.

briefs.title: The Boxes In The Hall
briefs.objective: Tell him he can’t move back in, without him hearing that she doesn’t want him.
briefs.obstacle: He’s frightened under the jokes, she wants him there as much as she doesn’t, and he has already unpacked the kettle.

briefs.title: The Spare Key
briefs.objective: Hand back the key and leave without being asked why she stayed away.
briefs.obstacle: He was there every day at the end, and he talks about her father as someone she didn’t know.

briefs.title: Last Thursday’s Refill
briefs.objective: Tell him the truth herself before the hospital does, and give him whatever he asks of her.
briefs.obstacle: He has come to thank her for staying late that night, he’s holding a gift, and every kind thing he says makes it harder to start.

briefs.title: The Household Count
briefs.objective: Get her to count two people in the flat, not three.
briefs.obstacle: Her badge records everything, her job and her family’s flat depend on her accuracy, and his grandmother keeps coughing.

briefs.title: The Approved Lesson
briefs.objective: Give him the true answer without the microphones recording it.
briefs.obstacle: The microphones catch every word, the boy may be a test, and thirty children are watching what she does.

briefs.title: The Bloom
briefs.objective: Get him to shut off the town’s water tonight.
briefs.obstacle: The lab results won’t come until Monday, the festival opens tomorrow, and what she saw sounds impossible.

briefs.title: The Warm Walls
briefs.objective: Get him out of that house before morning.
briefs.obstacle: He doesn’t want to leave, he says the walls are warm and that they listen, and the longer she stays in the house the less she wants to leave either.

demands.belongsTo: Battle and sword-and-sandal epics (warrior / swashbuckler leads)

briefs.title: The Ford Before Winter
briefs.objective: Make her delay the crossing until spring.
briefs.obstacle: She may not live to see the spring, she knows it, and she has never once been told no.

briefs.title: Muster At First Light
briefs.objective: Win her place back in the line.
briefs.obstacle: He gave the order himself to keep her home, she hasn’t carried a spear in twenty years, and he won’t let her die to prove a point.

briefs.title: The Second Key
briefs.objective: Find out whether he has the key without letting him know she’s looking.
briefs.obstacle: He’s suspicious of her too, the attraction is real, and whatever she learns, he learns about her.

briefs.title: Checkout At Noon
briefs.objective: End it tonight and walk out with her vote still her own.
briefs.obstacle: He has recordings of them, he’s calm about it, and part of her doesn’t want to go.

briefs.title: The Launderette
briefs.objective: Learn whether they’ll get him out before the arrests reach him.
briefs.obstacle: Asking means admitting fear, and fear makes a source a risk to be dropped.

briefs.title: The Routine Check
briefs.objective: Get on the plane as Hanna Wirth, whatever he says or knows.
briefs.obstacle: He knows her real name, his questions find the thin places in a cover she has worn for a year, and halfway through she can’t tell whether he’s warning her or working for the other side.

demands.belongsTo: dance film / choreocinema (screendance) strand of experimental film

briefs.title: The Glass Of Water
briefs.objective: Keep your words exactly the same while letting each new line change what they mean.
briefs.obstacle: You don’t know which line will change or how, and the same words have to answer four different situations.

briefs.title: Lots One To Forty
briefs.objective: Read the list exactly as written, and let the woman it describes come into the room.
briefs.obstacle: The words are an auctioneer’s, flat and priced, every lot has to be read as written, and the piece forbids any word that isn’t on the list.

briefs.title: Closed For The Season
briefs.objective: Get the photographs out of the glovebox without him knowing.
briefs.obstacle: He’s armed, he’s not a fool, and she has to keep his eyes on her while her hand finds the glovebox at her knee.

briefs.title: The Night Register
briefs.objective: Keep him away from the register and out of room 9 until he gives up and drives off.
briefs.obstacle: He’s charming and patient, his friends are waiting in the van, and he asks her to dance so he can read her face up close.

briefs.title: One Thing She Doesn’t Know
briefs.objective: Tell her one true thing she doesn’t know, and take her brother’s voice home.
briefs.obstacle: The woman already knows everything that has happened, to anyone, anywhere, and says so before Mette can finish.

briefs.title: The Lantern On The Ferry
briefs.objective: Stop the sale before the stranger comes back for his answer at midnight.
briefs.obstacle: Linnet thinks she’s dreaming, the lantern can speak only in rhyme, and the gold looks like the only way to keep the crossing.

briefs.title: The Treehouse Treaty
briefs.objective: Get her down and into bed without promising anything he can’t keep.
briefs.obstacle: She negotiates like a professional, and every demand on her list is one he wishes he could grant.

briefs.title: Career Day In Room Twelve
briefs.objective: Win the room, and make her son glad she came.
briefs.obstacle: Tilly asks every question her son was afraid of, one after another, the other children want the answers, and her son is watching from the back of the rug.

demands.belongsTo: particular productions with invented languages, and creature or motion-capture roles

briefs.title: The Cartographer’s Debt
briefs.objective: Settle the toll without unmaking the road her brother is still on.
briefs.obstacle: The keeper accepts only a road of equal length in payment, and every road she could give up has someone on it.

briefs.title: Inside A Minute
briefs.objective: Get the gate opened tonight, before the fever turns.
briefs.obstacle: Each bargain she strikes is gone within the minute, so the case has to be won again, and faster each time.

briefs.title: The Second Cake
briefs.objective: Get the cake out of the room before she reads it.
briefs.obstacle: She’s standing between him and the door, and she keeps turning toward the table.

briefs.title: The Sideways Presentation
briefs.objective: Get through the presentation without turning his back to the room.
briefs.obstacle: The chart is across the room, and the chairwoman keeps asking him to step up and point at it.

briefs.title: The Night Line
briefs.objective: Find out whether he knows she listened, without letting him learn that she did.
briefs.obstacle: He’s asking her the same question, more pleasantly than she can.

briefs.title: The Number He Left
briefs.objective: Keep Cal at the rooming house, believing she’s on her way, until the train pulls out.
briefs.obstacle: He knows her voice too well to be lied to for long, the minutes are running out, and something in his answers sounds wrong.

demands.belongsTo: Folk horror that stages its community ritual as performed folk song (The Wicker Man and films modelled on it)

briefs.title: The Last Sheaf
briefs.objective: Decline the honor kindly and get his keys back before dark.
briefs.obstacle: Refusing would insult the whole village, and she has his keys in her apron pocket.

briefs.title: Keeping The Name
briefs.objective: Get Hester to go home so she can grieve alone and say his name.
briefs.obstacle: Hester won’t leave the chair before the third dawn, and each time Nell starts toward the name, the old woman lays her hand flat on the table and waits.

briefs.title: Night Two At Juniper Creek
briefs.objective: Get him to pack up and leave now, without frightening him or their mother when she watches.
briefs.obstacle: He thinks she’s being dramatic for the camera, and she can’t stop filming without breaking her promise.

briefs.title: The Tape For Later
briefs.objective: Make a cheerful tape her future self will enjoy, and keep the withdrawal off it.
briefs.obstacle: Dana believes the tape is worthless unless it holds the truth, and she won’t stop recording or asking.

briefs.title: The Back Of The Bakery
briefs.objective: Keep Eddie out of what comes next.
briefs.obstacle: Danny holds every card, and he already knows what Eddie has been saying.

briefs.title: Terms For The Widow
briefs.objective: Get the payments for her boys guaranteed, and walk out of the parlor alive.
briefs.obstacle: He offers only what he offers any widow, and if he learns what she saw, she won’t need a pension.

demands.belongsTo: English-speaking leads who re-voiced themselves in post-synchronisation

briefs.title: The Dry Umbrella
briefs.objective: Make him take the umbrella seriously.
briefs.obstacle: It sounds absurd said aloud, and he’s more interested in how well she knew the victim.

briefs.title: Berth Fifteen
briefs.objective: Get the concierge to describe the visitor, down to the smallest detail she can recall.
briefs.obstacle: She’s frightened and proud, the filmed lips fix the length of every line, and the detail that matters comes last.

briefs.title: The Steward’s Ledger
briefs.objective: Get her to tell him who paid for him, and why.
briefs.obstacle: Her loyalty is to the house, and she seems to think he already knows.

briefs.title: The Locked Organ
briefs.objective: Keep the vicar in the house until midnight, so that one other living soul will hear it.
briefs.obstacle: The vicar believes Sir Ambrose plays it himself in his grief, and has come to counsel him gently, then go home.

demands.belongsTo: stunt performers in homage films

briefs.title: Last Gas For Ninety Miles
briefs.objective: Get the plate number to the dispatcher on the open line without him knowing she has.
briefs.obstacle: The phone is at her elbow, he’s watching her hands, and the knocking has stopped.

briefs.title: Paid In Quarters
briefs.objective: Keep her school, pay what she owes, and not a cent more.
briefs.obstacle: Lonnie has orders to come back with double or with the keys, and his two men are already moving.

demands.belongsTo: Linklater-style and mumblecore-adjacent naturalistic hangout films

briefs.title: Sunday At The Laundromat
briefs.objective: Tell her about the move.
briefs.obstacle: The afternoon is too good to spoil, and Bec keeps making her laugh.

briefs.title: No Meteors Tonight
briefs.objective: Keep Walt on the roof until the clouds clear.
briefs.obstacle: He has an early start, says so every ten minutes, and then thinks of one more thing to say.

briefs.title: The Walkthrough
briefs.objective: Get him to accept the changed rotation without telling him why she changed it.
briefs.obstacle: He trusts the plan more than he trusts her, and any change this late looks like a setup.

briefs.title: The Last Number
briefs.objective: Open the safe and get them both clear before the patrol comes round again.
briefs.obstacle: The last tumbler falls too quietly for him to hear now, and Tess’s reports from the street change by the minute.

demands.belongsTo: British period productions that ask for period Received Pronunciation

briefs.title: Across Her Own Key
briefs.objective: Deliver it properly, the way she’d want it done for anyone, and stay on her feet.
briefs.obstacle: June knows the moment she sees the envelope, and Margaret’s grief is the same as hers.

briefs.title: Before The Parade
briefs.objective: Get the parade called off tonight.
briefs.obstacle: The parade is his pride and the war effort’s, the governor is coming, and to him calling it off sounds like giving up on the boys overseas.

demands.belongsTo: dance: period stories with social-dance scenes (court, Regency, costume romance); heightened: adaptations of period dramatic texts (Shakespeare, Restoration comedy) or scripts written in period verse or rhetoric

briefs.title: Proof Of Birth
briefs.objective: Be believed, and leave with the paper signed.
briefs.obstacle: The clerk asks small questions he can’t prepare for: which church bell he heard as a boy, what the corner store sold.

briefs.title: One Book From The Fire
briefs.objective: Confess his part in the loss, and give his master a reason to begin again.
briefs.obstacle: The old man won’t speak or look at him, and one small book is so little beside what was lost.

briefs.title: The Last Thanksgiving Plate
briefs.objective: Give him a good last Thanksgiving here, and tell him herself.
briefs.obstacle: He’s so pleased to see her that the news feels cruel, and he has brought her a card, as he does every year.

briefs.title: The Closing Announcement
briefs.objective: Get Danny to walk to the service desk on his own.
briefs.obstacle: He thinks he’s in trouble for breaking a snow globe, he won’t answer in words, and she can’t see him.

briefs.title: The Summer Program
briefs.objective: Get Andre’s blessing, and his word that he’ll stay with Grandma.
briefs.obstacle: Andre came home to be with family, and the first thing his family tells him is that it’s leaving.

briefs.title: The Toast For Daniela
briefs.objective: Win his grandmother’s approval of the toast before the doors open.
briefs.obstacle: She wants it to sound like his father, he can’t be his father, and every time she stops him the cards get worse.

demands.belongsTo: chase-and-struggle roles (see slasher’s final girl)

briefs.title: Someone Behind You
briefs.objective: Get out of the front door, guided only by his voice.
briefs.obstacle: She can’t look and can’t run without turning, and he can see it move whenever she moves.

briefs.title: Chapter Nine
briefs.objective: Read her way to a page she isn’t on.
briefs.obstacle: The chapter describes each thing she does a line before she does it, and it says that if the narrator stops reading, she’ll hear the booth door open.

briefs.title: The Open House
briefs.objective: Get the offer signed before the house frightens him off.
briefs.obstacle: The house slams doors, drops the temperature and writes on the mirror, and she’s the only one who sees it.

briefs.title: The Story She Made Up
briefs.objective: Get the campers off the porch and into the dining hall without frightening them.
briefs.obstacle: Owen won’t move until he hears the ending, he catches every change she makes to the story, and the thing in the trees comes closer whenever she stops talking.

readings.label: The Best She Ever Told It

briefs.title: Level One, Again
briefs.objective: Work out the rules of this world before the villagers come for her.
briefs.obstacle: The panel answers every question with a cheerful note about her progress, and nothing she knows seems to apply here.

briefs.title: Dialogue Option Three
briefs.objective: Make Bram leave the inn before tonight, when the script says it burns.
briefs.obstacle: He can answer only with the lines she gave him, and she gave him six.

briefs.title: The Petition For Vengeance
briefs.objective: Leave with the license sealed.
briefs.obstacle: He holds that a widow owes her house its heir before its honor, and every refusal comes in a courtesy she has to match.

briefs.title: The Small Door In The Ward Gate
briefs.objective: Get the young man through the side door and on his way home, with the great gate shut and no blood on the street.
briefs.obstacle: The young man won’t stoop for any door, his hand is on his sword, and a townsman who strikes a samurai, even to save his own life, can be put to death for it.

briefs.title: The Reunion Set
briefs.objective: Get him to sing the harmony with her, the way they used to.
briefs.obstacle: He’s embarrassed, the room is watching, and he can’t tell whether she’s mocking him.

briefs.title: The Resignation Number
briefs.objective: Quit, and for once make him react.
briefs.obstacle: He reacts to nothing, and the song is coming whether she wants it or not.

demands.belongsTo: the suit actor playing the creature

briefs.title: Tell Me What It Looks Like
briefs.objective: Get him registered and the line moving.
briefs.obstacle: He won’t budge, the floor keeps shaking, and to describe the thing she has to look at it.

briefs.title: The Footprint Shop
briefs.objective: Stay in her shop and see it once more.
briefs.obstacle: He has orders to clear the seafront, he won’t leave without her, and he doesn’t believe a creature like that can be beautiful.

briefs.title: Not Going Back
briefs.objective: Get his mother on his side before his father walks in.
briefs.obstacle: She already knows, she’s frightened for him, and the wage he walked away from paid the rent.

briefs.title: One More Friday
briefs.objective: Keep the house for one more week, without telling him where the money went.
briefs.obstacle: He has heard every excuse in the street, the landlord wants the house back, and the neighbor will hear whatever she says.

briefs.title: The Recess
briefs.objective: Make sure she understands why the plea is the surer justice, and hear her out, before the clock runs out.
briefs.obstacle: She wants the man convicted of murder, and the honest reason for the plea is that the state might lose.

briefs.title: Just The Radiator
briefs.objective: Get her ready to tell the truth simply, and to hold up under the other side’s questions.
briefs.obstacle: She embroiders every telling to help, she can’t see why the plain truth would be enough, and his practice cross-examination frightens her more than he meant it to.

briefs.title: The Back Bedroom
briefs.objective: Get him to sign off the visit without sending anyone to fix the rain.
briefs.obstacle: His job is to stop water coming into houses, and he keeps reaching for the practical answer.

briefs.title: Postmarked Thursday
briefs.objective: Get him to open the envelope on the doorstep today, so his sister goes on to write it.
briefs.obstacle: He refuses to read words his sister hasn’t chosen yet, and he gives the carrier almost nothing but a door held half shut.

briefs.title: The Return Bow
briefs.objective: Get through the round with every strike under control, so he takes her back.
briefs.obstacle: He keeps naming the night at the bar while they spar, and he calls openings she could take.

briefs.title: Level Six, After Midnight
briefs.objective: End the challenge with him still on his feet and willing to visit her father in the hospital.
briefs.obstacle: He came for a winner and hits to hurt, and holding back against him could cost her the school.

briefs.title: Handover At Seven
briefs.objective: Get him to examine the patient now, before rounds.
briefs.obstacle: Every single reading is defensible, she’s exhausted, and she can’t prove what she’s afraid of.

briefs.title: First Touch, Bay Four
briefs.objective: Get his hands through the ports and resting on his daughter before the shift changes.
briefs.obstacle: He’s sure he’ll hurt her or set off an alarm, and each time she nearly has him, he pushes back with another question about the monitors.

briefs.title: The Sewing Box
briefs.objective: Keep her daughter from getting on that train.
briefs.obstacle: The daughter is ready for anger, and the one argument that might reach her is the secret the mother has kept all her life.

briefs.title: The Housekeeper’s Keys
briefs.objective: Make the housekeeper renounce the will and quit the house before morning.
briefs.obstacle: The housekeeper won’t defend herself or go, and the reason she’s guarding is the one the heiress least wants to hear.

demands.belongsTo: combat films with an adviser’s boot camp (see war)

briefs.title: Box Seven
briefs.objective: Get the box filled in with a real name before he leaves the office.
briefs.obstacle: He says there’s nobody to put, and he’d rather be shouted at than asked why.

briefs.title: Twelve Minutes Home
briefs.objective: Give her daughter a birthday call that sounds like an ordinary day.
briefs.obstacle: The lag swallows every joke, the clock is running, and her wife hears the strain on the first hello.

briefs.title: Pool Manager Of The Year
briefs.objective: Get the award story back on track and the drained pool out of the film.
briefs.obstacle: The producer keeps returning to yesterday, and the camera keeps rolling through every pause.

briefs.title: Room Three Opens At Seven
briefs.objective: Get a finished, working room on film before the party starts.
briefs.obstacle: The final padlock won’t take the code, and the only person who knows why is the brother-in-law she fired last week.

demands.belongsTo: the performer in the creature suit

briefs.title: The Pump House
briefs.objective: Keep him on the platform and silent until it moves on.
briefs.obstacle: She can only whisper, he doesn’t believe her, and the water below keeps shifting.

briefs.title: Aisle Eleven
briefs.objective: Get him up and across the floor to the stockroom before the thing finishes at the far end.
briefs.obstacle: He can hardly stand, he wants to stay hidden, and every route to the steel door crosses the end of an aisle it can see down.

briefs.title: The Second Bedroom
briefs.objective: Get the news said before the food runs out.
briefs.obstacle: Jules keeps talking, she keeps letting her, and saying it out loud makes it real.

briefs.title: Allen Key
briefs.objective: Find out, without asking straight out, whether the “and guest” on the invitation means her.
briefs.obstacle: He answers every question sideways, and a direct question would make this a relationship.

briefs.title: Last Frame At The Bluebird Lanes
briefs.objective: Make him hear what the place is before he sells it.
briefs.obstacle: The sale is signed, he’s embarrassed by feeling, and he wants to be home.

briefs.title: Everything You Ever Spilled
briefs.objective: Tell her, before she leaves, that he’ll miss her.
briefs.obstacle: He can only say it the way he knows her, through her stains, and she has a taxi coming.

briefs.title: The Wrong Peg
briefs.objective: Find out why his coat was by the vestry door.
briefs.obstacle: He’s her friend, he’s charming, and asking outright means accusing him.

briefs.title: The Back Of The Canvas
briefs.objective: Prove to the director that she didn’t make the swap, before the police arrive at nine.
briefs.obstacle: The alarm log points at her, the director wants a confession, and the only proof she can find names the man who taught her to paint.

briefs.title: The Last Pool
briefs.objective: Carry the viewer through the sequence so they feel the dry season end.
briefs.obstacle: The lines are fixed to the shots, and the story has to live inside the time each picture allows.

briefs.title: The Haypile
briefs.objective: Make the children cheer for the pika by the time the snow falls.
briefs.obstacle: The shots are fast and short, the lines must fit them exactly, and the hawk has to frighten without upsetting a six-year-old.

demands.belongsTo: The narrating lead in neo-noirs that retain classic noir's first-person voice-over

briefs.title: Lost Property
briefs.objective: Find out what the money is before she decides what she’ll say about it.
briefs.obstacle: He’s pleasant and patient, he’s offering her a share, and he knows exactly how much she needs it.

briefs.title: What The Night Desk Saw
briefs.objective: Tell the story straight to the end without admitting what she knew when she handed him the key.
briefs.obstacle: The pictures keep showing the part she leaves out, and the narration has to sound like it believes itself.

demands.belongsTo: non-professional casting, which is the casting’s, not a technique asked of an actor

briefs.title: The Sewing Machine
briefs.objective: Get enough for the doctor and the promise that the machine stays on the shelf until she can buy it back.
briefs.obstacle: He offers less than the doctor’s bill, and he has never held anything for anyone.

briefs.title: The Bricks Of Number Nine
briefs.objective: Leave the site with this morning’s stack, or at least with the guard’s silence until tomorrow.
briefs.obstacle: On paper the bricks belong to the city, whatever they were before, and the guard has his orders and a family of his own.

briefs.title: The Night Train South
briefs.objective: Get him on the train with her tonight.
briefs.obstacle: He likes her, and he has an exam, a mother and a whole careful life.

briefs.title: Five Minutes Before The Lights
briefs.objective: Get into the late show without paying.
briefs.obstacle: He has a rule, a manager in the back office, and a taste for arguments that he’ll gladly keep going past the start of the film.

briefs.title: The Ferry Timetable
briefs.objective: Get him to tell her what he saw on the night the woman left.
briefs.obstacle: He has a reason to be afraid of whoever was with her, and she keeps filling the silences he needs before he can answer.

briefs.title: The Mine Road
briefs.objective: Get him to say who was really driving, so she doesn’t have to charge him.
briefs.obstacle: He has learned his statement by heart, he won’t look at her, and the truth would put his mother in prison.

demands.belongsTo: Possession / exorcism films: the possessed role and the voice of the possessing entity

briefs.title: The Locked Room At Aunt Bea’s
briefs.objective: Open the room and get the house cleared, so it can be sold.
briefs.obstacle: Her uncle is frightened in a way she’s never seen, and something on the other side of the door has just moved.

briefs.title: Lot Two Hundred And Six
briefs.objective: Stop reading before the last verse, without losing the sale.
briefs.obstacle: Her director needs the money to keep the doors open, the bidder is listening on the line, and every verse she reads is answered by a door, a footstep, a light.

briefs.title: The Big Speech
briefs.objective: Inspire the team to win the next round.
briefs.obstacle: The captain keeps correcting his chess, and the speech has nothing to do with the game.

briefs.title: Trash Day: The Trailer
briefs.objective: Make a fight about recycling sound like the most important story ever told.
briefs.obstacle: The pictures are a bin, a sticky note and a tenants’ meeting, and the joke dies the moment the voice admits it.

briefs.title: The Gown For Tonight
briefs.objective: Leave the shop with the dressmaker’s word that the gown will be right and delivered by seven.
briefs.obstacle: A maid may not accuse a tradeswoman of error, may not mention her mistress’s debts, and may not go home without the gown.

briefs.title: The Tenancy Of Low Fold
briefs.objective: Walk out of the office with the lease in her own name.
briefs.obstacle: The estate has never let a farm to a woman, the agent keeps pressing a cottage and a pension on her instead, and the cousin’s signature is already dry.

briefs.title: The Guesser Of Weights
briefs.objective: Get the job, and the advance on the day’s wages, before he finds anyone else.
briefs.obstacle: He tests her on the spot by asking her to guess his weight, and she has no idea.

briefs.title: Notes From The Overnight Bus
briefs.objective: Get her to offer him the spare room for a week, without his ever having to ask.
briefs.obstacle: She has heard versions of these stories all her life, the battery is dying, and asking outright would mean admitting the year has beaten him.

briefs.title: The Sign-Out Sheet
briefs.objective: Get the gap recorded honestly, even though it puts her partner and the case at risk.
briefs.obstacle: The clerk would rather fill the gap in now and say nothing, and the defense will use it if they don’t.

briefs.title: Six Folders
briefs.objective: Get an identification, or an honest no, that will stand up in court.
briefs.obstacle: He keeps asking which one it is, reading her face for a clue, and any sign from her can throw the whole lineup out.

briefs.title: Forty Votes
briefs.objective: Get her to make the concession call tonight, before the volunteers hear it from someone else.
briefs.obstacle: Bianca believes the count is wrong, and Lorna can’t prove it isn’t.

briefs.title: The Vote On Ridge Line
briefs.objective: Get the room to hear her reasons all the way through before Monday.
briefs.obstacle: The room is against her, the man who drove her to school is leading the heckling, and her own staff told her not to come.

briefs.title: Who Had A Copy
briefs.objective: Brief him fully and fairly without giving herself away.
briefs.obstacle: He’s watching her closely, he’s been good to her, and her own name has to be on the list.

briefs.title: Booth C
briefs.objective: Get through the statement without betraying either the speaker or her own side.
briefs.obstacle: The interpretation can’t stop, there’s no time to think, and whatever she says in the third paragraph, everyone in the hall will hear it.

demands.belongsTo: stunt: action-led post-apocalyptic films (Mad Max lineage); transformation: individual starving-survivor lead roles

briefs.title: Channel Sixteen
briefs.objective: Find out whether she’s genuine without telling her where the settlement is.
briefs.obstacle: Every word he sends can be followed back to his people, and she isn’t asking for herself.

briefs.title: The First Lesson
briefs.objective: Get him to read one word by the end of the hour, so he comes back tomorrow.
briefs.obstacle: He sees no use in reading, there’s a fence to mend, and he gives her almost nothing to start from.

briefs.title: Table Nine
briefs.objective: Keep her talking long enough to be her father for an hour.
briefs.obstacle: She came for a signature, and the form asks him to give up his name.

briefs.title: First Night On The Tier
briefs.objective: Get him to give the packet back tomorrow morning, before the man on the tier comes to collect.
briefs.obstacle: The kid thinks he’s found a friend, he doesn’t trust a cellmate he met six hours ago, and the older man has sworn to stay out of other people’s business.

briefs.title: Ten Past Four
briefs.objective: Make him believe her before he asks her to come home and see someone.
briefs.obstacle: Every fact she gives him has an ordinary explanation, and she’s not certain anymore that he’s wrong.

briefs.title: Night Log, Day Nine
briefs.objective: Record a calm, sensible log, so the clinic clears her to go back to work.
briefs.obstacle: She can’t explain last night’s file, the harder she tries to sound sensible the stranger it sounds, and she can’t be sure she’s awake.

briefs.title: The Rehung Frames
briefs.objective: Make him admit he’s been coming in and moving the frames.
briefs.obstacle: He has a message from her number, sent last Tuesday, asking him to come and straighten the frames, and she has no memory of sending it.

briefs.title: The Overnight Study
briefs.objective: Keep him talking until she understands how he knows, without letting him hear that she’s frightened.
briefs.obstacle: The monitors insist he’s in deep sleep, he answers her questions after long silences, and the supervisor’s phone goes unanswered every time she tries it.

briefs.title: The Toast
briefs.objective: Get through the toast once without stopping, so Yusra will say it’s good.
briefs.obstacle: The middle of the toast is about how you know you’ve found your person, and the person she wrote it about is sitting right there.

briefs.title: The Plaque In The Trophy Case
briefs.objective: Leave the office with his signature on the engraver’s form, so the plaque reads Rosalind by the spring banquet.
briefs.obstacle: A change to a plaque has to go before the league board, Hank is afraid of what two of its members will say, and he hates to admit it to her.

demands.belongsTo: revenge action films and their fight-trained leads

briefs.title: The Retirement Folder
briefs.objective: Make him remember what he did before she decides what to do with the folder.
briefs.obstacle: He’s kind, and genuinely can’t place her father’s name.

briefs.title: The Dealer’s Last Hand
briefs.objective: Win back the deed to her diner in a single hand, and make him remember whose it was.
briefs.obstacle: He stacked a deck against her once and watches for the same trick in everyone, he’s demanded a fresh deck, and he pushes at her with every card.

briefs.title: Mile Marker 212
briefs.objective: Find out why he wants to turn back, so she can talk him out of it.
briefs.obstacle: She has to keep her eyes on the road, and he answers every question with a question about her.

briefs.title: One More State
briefs.objective: Talk Bernadette into one more state before she flies home.
briefs.obstacle: Bernadette has a granddaughter counting on her and a life she likes, and Connie can’t bring herself to ask outright.

demands.belongsTo: The mock rockumentary (This Is Spinal Tap and its imitators): improvisation for the whole cast, song for the actor-musicians in the band roles

briefs.title: The Long Version
briefs.objective: Tell the story the way she always has, and finish the interview with it intact.
briefs.obstacle: The filmmaker reads her the letter, signed in her hand, and waits.

briefs.title: Soundcheck At The Granary
briefs.objective: Get Dot onto the stage for the soundcheck before the doors open at seven.
briefs.obstacle: Dot won’t sing that song again, and the one thing that might change her mind is something Marisol has never said, least of all with a camera running.

briefs.title: One Stem On Fridays
briefs.objective: Find out who the flowers have been for before she leaves.
briefs.obstacle: He’s shy, and every time she gets near the question he talks about the flowers.

briefs.title: Thursday Beginners
briefs.objective: Ask her to Saturday’s social as his date, and get a yes she means.
briefs.obstacle: She thinks he’s asking her to partner him in the demonstration waltz, and every time he tries to set it straight she says yes to the wrong thing.

briefs.title: The Parrot Knows
briefs.objective: Get the key without admitting the date mattered to her.
briefs.obstacle: He wants to talk about the date first, and through the door the parrot repeats something she said about him on the phone.

briefs.title: Table Six, Three Minutes
briefs.objective: Keep the three minutes light, move on to table seven, and win the fifty dollars with her dignity intact.
briefs.obstacle: He keeps the questions coming, he knows her mouth better than anyone alive, and now that she can finally talk back she finds she’s enjoying it.

briefs.title: The House Sale
briefs.objective: Tell him she was wrong to send him away.
briefs.obstacle: He’s happy, and saying it would cost him something he doesn’t owe her.

briefs.title: The Twelve-Minute Window
briefs.objective: Tell her about the job and hear what she really thinks before the link drops.
briefs.obstacle: Every answer reaches him two seconds late, so he can’t tell her pauses from the delay, and she has news of her own she’s been saving for this call.

briefs.title: The Crossing At Dawn
briefs.objective: Bring Sakon back alive, by his own consent if possible.
briefs.obstacle: Sakon won’t go back, and the order leaves Gonroku no honorable way to let him pass.

briefs.title: The First Form
briefs.objective: Learn why she has chosen him, and answer her honestly, before he accepts the boy or refuses him.
briefs.obstacle: She gives away almost nothing, and whatever her reason, teaching the boy means one day telling him how his father died.

rows.label: Satire

demands.belongsTo: Character-comedian satire (Sellers in Dr. Strangelove; improvised character-prank satire)

playsOfKind: The Playboy Of The Western World

briefs.title: The Contentment Index
briefs.objective: Get her to withdraw the complaint so the street’s score recovers by Friday.
briefs.obstacle: She doesn’t care about the score; she wants the hole filled before someone breaks an ankle.

briefs.title: The Monday Announcements
briefs.objective: Read the week’s announcements word for word in the brand voice, as he has every Monday for nineteen years.
briefs.obstacle: The last paragraph announces, in the same cheerful words as the rest, that from Friday the morning announcements and the assistant manager’s post will be handled by an automated voice.

briefs.title: The Messenger In The Shrine
briefs.objective: Get the power cell without breaking the village’s faith.
briefs.obstacle: Mother Ibbet knows exactly what the drone is, and wants something for it.

briefs.title: Spoken Into Force
briefs.objective: Speak the treaty into force without binding anyone to more than her queen agreed to.
briefs.obstacle: The envoy’s device renders its clauses into the old tongue loosely, and one phrase, said aloud, would bind every child born in the kingdom to the Combine’s service.

briefs.title: Eight Years Out
briefs.objective: Be her father again in this one conversation.
briefs.obstacle: She grew up without him, and she’s polite to him the way you’re polite to a guest.

briefs.title: Statement For The Backup
briefs.objective: Tell the woman who might wake who she is, so she can take up Noor’s life without being frightened by it.
briefs.obstacle: She has four minutes and no script, and she can’t decide whether to ask the copy to be her or to be someone new.

briefs.title: The Wardrobe In Suite Nine
briefs.objective: Get him out of the suite before the dog barks.
briefs.obstacle: He’s sure she’s hiding something, and he isn’t leaving until he finds out what.

briefs.title: Night Board At The Halloway
briefs.objective: Keep the board running, and her fiancé off her trail, until the party gives up and goes home.
briefs.obstacle: She has no idea how a switchboard works, her fiancé keeps ringing down for the operator, and Leo has started to notice her pearls.

briefs.title: Below The Waterline
briefs.objective: Make him bring the ship’s head into the wind before the mast goes.
briefs.obstacle: He can’t see the crack from where he stands, and turning costs him a day he’s promised the owners.

briefs.title: Twenty-Two Days Becalmed
briefs.objective: Keep the cask locked until the wind comes, without the crew breaking into the hold.
briefs.obstacle: The men are dying of thirst by inches, the bosun is right that another cup each would save the weakest, and Elias can’t promise them wind.

briefs.title: The Telegram For Miss Avery
briefs.objective: Decide what to do with the telegram before she reaches the counter.
briefs.obstacle: He has a few seconds and no words, and everything he feels has to show in his face and hands.

briefs.title: Her First Sitting Alone
briefs.objective: Sit for a portrait her daughter will want to keep.
briefs.obstacle: She’s never been photographed alone, every pose she tries looks to her like someone else’s, and she can’t say any of it aloud.

briefs.title: The Last Strip
briefs.objective: Hang the last strip before the guests come in.
briefs.obstacle: The strip sticks to everything but the wall, and a wasp comes in through the open window.

briefs.title: The Enchanted Folding Chair
briefs.objective: Get through every trick looking as if he meant it, for his daughter in the front row.
briefs.obstacle: Every prop is rigged to fail on the volunteer, the magician improvises the order, and fourteen children laugh hardest when he gets hurt.

demands.belongsTo: the final girl

briefs.title: Last Night Of The Season
briefs.objective: Keep the dispatcher on the line and get a car sent.
briefs.obstacle: He thinks it’s kids from the maze playing a joke, and every time she raises her voice the footsteps outside stop.

briefs.title: Inside The Walk-In
briefs.objective: Keep Danny quiet and get them both out the back before the cold or the man outside gets to them.
briefs.obstacle: Danny panics in waves and gets loud, the only way out runs through the kitchen, and the cold gets further into them by the minute.

briefs.title: The Late Number Nine
briefs.objective: Finish the essay paragraph before the bus comes.
briefs.obstacle: Mr. Sadowski needs the card written, and then wants it signed the way his late wife always signed them.

briefs.title: The Walking Tour, Track Seven
briefs.objective: Read Track Seven as written and inside ninety seconds, so the intern’s script gets used.
briefs.obstacle: Every line about the brickwork reminds him of something that happened behind it, and the true stories are better than the script.

demands.belongsTo: Ken Loach’s productions and those that work his way

briefs.title: Between Clients
briefs.objective: Leave with a promise that the travel time will be paid.
briefs.obstacle: The policy was set by the owners, and Bev can offer only sympathy and a tote bag from the agency’s appreciation week.

briefs.title: Proof Of Employer
briefs.objective: Get the week’s groceries and get out without having to say aloud that a full-time wage doesn’t feed his family.
briefs.obstacle: The form has to be filled in, Gwen has to ask every question on it, and she gives him so little that he can’t tell what she thinks of him.

briefs.title: The Blockade At Corvane
briefs.objective: Get her sister to let the freighter through the jump point.
briefs.obstacle: Folake will let it pass only if Reva hands over the rebels’ leader, who is on board and is a child’s grandmother.

briefs.title: Stand Down At Halcyon Gate
briefs.objective: Bring all forty ships to stand down, so that no captain fires a shot after the war is over.
briefs.obstacle: Every word she says to her own people is heard by the enemy, the three captains who mean to fight on are listening for a hint she wants them to, and pride is all her crews have left.

demands.belongsTo: Sergio Leone’s films

briefs.title: The Relay Station At Dry Fork
briefs.objective: Send him on with a fresh horse and nothing else.
briefs.obstacle: He’s patient, and he has seen the fresh tracks.

briefs.title: Three Shares At The Mission
briefs.objective: Count out three shares and ride away with the third for Eli’s widow, whatever Silas says about it.
briefs.obstacle: Silas wants half, he’s standing nearer the horses, and he’s faster with a gun than she is.

briefs.title: Paint Department
briefs.objective: Get him to sell her a gallon of bleach and forget he saw her.
briefs.obstacle: He opens the door, and she’s red to the elbows.

briefs.title: Two Heartbeats In The Straw
briefs.objective: Get the vet out to the farm tonight without having to say aloud what she killed.
briefs.obstacle: He decided from her first sentence that it’s a calf, no vet drives out at one in the morning for a dead calf, and every check on his list shows her something worse.

demands.belongsTo: combat-sport films such as boxing films

briefs.title: The Last Lap
briefs.objective: Get Liv to agree to follow her pace and kick at the bell.
briefs.obstacle: Liv won’t take a gift from her in her last race.

briefs.title: The Assessor’s Report
briefs.objective: Write a report she can sign and still be the referee she believes she is.
briefs.obstacle: The honest report could cost her the international list, and Victor keeps pressing her to write that her view was blocked.

briefs.title: Two Coffees
briefs.objective: Keep her cover without telling him a lie she’ll have to remember.
briefs.obstacle: He isn’t suspicious, only curious, and he asks the questions a husband would.

briefs.title: Group Four Seven
briefs.objective: Read the sheet exactly, at the cadence, so the warning reaches him clean.
briefs.obstacle: The studio is monitored and any break in the cadence is logged, and every listener on the frequency, friend or not, hears her voice.

briefs.title: The Pressure Certificate
briefs.objective: Get the certificate stamped without showing him the valves.
briefs.obstacle: The gauge reads above the limit, and he won’t stamp anything he can’t explain.

briefs.title: Forty-One Turns
briefs.objective: Learn to wind the regulator well enough to trust her own hands at midnight tomorrow, alone.
briefs.obstacle: Her hands shake, the count has to be exact, and part of her still believes the man teaching her should never have done it.

briefs.title: The Wrong Couch
briefs.objective: Get out with his dignity and his left shoe, which he can’t find.
briefs.obstacle: His thinking keeps arriving a sentence late, and every true thing he says makes it sound worse.

briefs.title: The Call With Her Father
briefs.objective: Make a good impression on the man whose blessing his girlfriend wants.
briefs.obstacle: The brownies arrive in waves, time stretches between one question and the next, and the father notices everything.

briefs.title: Holding Breath
briefs.objective: Get the device away from him without hurting him and without him seeing how much it costs her.
briefs.obstacle: Her hold lasts only as long as her breath, and he knows it, because she told him once when they were kids.

briefs.title: The Bakery On Calder Street
briefs.objective: Get the fund to pay for the bakery’s new front by Friday.
briefs.obstacle: The form allows for “reasonable force,” and every move she shows him looks less reasonable than she remembered.

briefs.title: The Kettle At Six
briefs.objective: Get him to drive out tonight without sounding like she’s losing her mind.
briefs.obstacle: He’s gentle about it. That makes it worse, and she can’t say the thing she’s afraid of without hearing how it sounds.

briefs.title: Reading To The Corner
briefs.objective: Persuade the boy to leave his daughter alone at night.
briefs.obstacle: He can’t see the boy, the boy gives him almost nothing, and the more he learns the less he wants to send him away.

briefs.title: The Interview In The Wet Office
briefs.objective: Get the job by giving the right answers.
briefs.obstacle: There are no right answers she can find, and the questions keep reaching something true.

briefs.title: The Third Day Of Applause
briefs.objective: Get the audience to stop so she can go home and sleep.
briefs.obstacle: Every bow she takes makes them louder, his remedies are worse than hers, and part of her has wanted this since she was eight.

briefs.title: Four Percent
briefs.objective: Give her his position clearly enough that a crew can find him before the battery dies.
briefs.obstacle: The cold has slowed his thinking, he can’t see out, and every word he spends on anything else costs battery.

briefs.title: The Fuel Line
briefs.objective: Get his permission to go out before the backup runs dry.
briefs.obstacle: He has the authority to forbid it, he has good reasons, and every minute they argue costs fuel.

readings.label: The Job In Front Of Her

briefs.title: The Customs House Stair
briefs.objective: Keep him on the stair until the harbor bell rings the tide.
briefs.obstacle: He’s better than he was, and if he disarms her he’ll go straight to the quay.

briefs.title: The Steward Of The Cellar
briefs.objective: Get out of the cellar with the papers before the watch changes at one.
briefs.obstacle: He’s better with a sword than she is, and every trick she tries he seems to have seen before.

briefs.title: The Games Account
briefs.objective: Make him take back the promise without shaming him.
briefs.obstacle: The boy’s pride, and the town’s expectation that the old champion will lift the bronze in the forum once more as part of the show.

briefs.title: The Second Answer
briefs.objective: Keep him and his forty men out of the valley tomorrow, without telling a lie in the god’s name.
briefs.obstacle: He wants only a yes, he has a drawn sword and a short temper, and the truth she can give him comes from his own words, not from any vision.

briefs.title: The Bridge Toll
briefs.objective: Cross the bridge and keep the memory.
briefs.obstacle: He’s stronger, the bridge sways under them, and the toll is the one thing she won’t pay.

briefs.title: The Last Night On Guard
briefs.objective: Walk out of the tower at dawn with her contract ended and her will still her own.
briefs.obstacle: Every shape he raises is a fight she has to win again, he knows exactly which ones hurt, and part of her doesn’t want to leave him to his enemies.

briefs.title: The Dosing Pump
briefs.objective: Keep the town’s water safe, whatever that does to his trace.
briefs.obstacle: If she pulls the plant off the network she loses the remote sensors and the evidence, and he’s telling her not to.

briefs.title: Three Of Five
briefs.objective: Stop the signing before his card goes in, without saying on camera what she fears, in case whoever is pressing him is watching the stream.
briefs.obstacle: The script leaves no room for talk off the page, he gives her nothing, and a halt needs a reason she can say aloud to the auditors without naming him.

briefs.title: The Permission Slip
briefs.objective: Get to go to the competition without saying sorry.
briefs.obstacle: Her mother says she’d have signed it if she had been asked, and that takes away every argument Anjali prepared.

briefs.title: Past The Deadline
briefs.objective: Get her name onto the running order before it goes to the printer.
briefs.obstacle: He has heard every excuse, he’s already late, and the only argument he’ll take is the poem itself, a thing she has only ever said in her head.

briefs.title: The Night Hatch
briefs.objective: Keep him at the hatch until the police come, without letting him see that she knows.
briefs.obstacle: He’s watching her face, and every minute the prescription takes is a minute he might wonder why.

briefs.title: The Empty Slot
briefs.objective: Get the true story out of him before anyone else asks for it.
briefs.obstacle: He lies to her, he’s her son, and she isn’t sure she wants to hear what he might say.

demands.belongsTo: roles playing another actor's character at a different age (past/future self)

briefs.title: The Ninth Afternoon
briefs.objective: Keep him off the stairs this time.
briefs.obstacle: Everything she says to stop him is what sends him there.

briefs.title: Ninety Seconds To Nineteen
briefs.objective: Get her younger self through that night without changing anything that matters.
briefs.obstacle: Every warning she tries is silenced by the machine, and she has only ninety seconds and one take.

demands.belongsTo: the suit actor

briefs.title: The Observation Tower
briefs.objective: Get the strike called off long enough for the creature to take the egg back to sea.
briefs.obstacle: She’s the most junior person on the channel, and everything she can report sounds like what a frightened recruit would want to believe.

briefs.title: The Voice In The Armor
briefs.objective: Get Jin to stand down and come home without striking the last blow.
briefs.obstacle: Jin begs him to finish it, and every word has to land inside a suited body’s movements that were fixed months ago.

demands.belongsTo: classical verse tragedy, which a play’s own reads carry (Macbeth reads Classical Text at 3)

briefs.title: The Floodgates
briefs.objective: Tell him the truth and keep his love, if both are possible.
briefs.obstacle: They aren’t both possible, and she knows it before she begins.

briefs.title: The Steady Hand
briefs.objective: Get him to scrub in beside her and do what he has always done, so she can save the boy herself.
briefs.obstacle: He has never refused her before, the hand is shaking tonight, and the only other surgeon who could try is two hours away.

briefs.title: Three Minutes
briefs.objective: Get the eulogy to three minutes without cutting the parts that were her.
briefs.obstacle: All the parts that were her are the funny ones, and they’re the ones she suggests cutting.

briefs.title: The Soup Lesson
briefs.objective: Teach his son the soup, all of it, while he still has all of it.
briefs.obstacle: His memory slips without warning, and his son keeps noticing.

demands.belongsTo: Dramatised true crime roles portraying real people whose speech differs from the actor's own

briefs.title: The Register At The Starlite
briefs.objective: Tell the story the way she always has and get through the interview.
briefs.obstacle: The register shows a second signature in a hand she knows, and the producer is waiting for her to see it.

briefs.title: A Correction, Episode Nine
briefs.objective: Undo, as far as words can, what her show did to an innocent man.
briefs.obstacle: Her listeners loved the story she told, a correction is duller than an accusation, and her own voice keeps slipping back into the show’s storytelling tone.

briefs.title: The Threshold
briefs.objective: Be invited in before the sun rises.
briefs.obstacle: She knows what he is and what he did the night he changed, and she won’t say the word until he tells her the truth about it.

briefs.title: Nights At The Blood Bank
briefs.objective: Get the job without telling her what he is.
briefs.obstacle: Every honest answer sounds stranger than a lie, and the cut on her finger is two feet from him.

briefs.title: The Culvert
briefs.objective: Stop the bleeding in his leg before it kills him.
briefs.obstacle: He thinks she means to kill him, and he’s reaching for her sidearm.

briefs.title: The Bell Tower
briefs.objective: Bring the guns down on the column in the square before it moves out toward the river.
briefs.obstacle: The radio keeps dropping, the square is her own town, and the boots on the stairs are getting closer.

demands.belongsTo: the werewolf role in practical-effects productions

briefs.title: The Cold Store
briefs.objective: Get his promise that he won’t open the door before morning.
briefs.obstacle: He has never been able to refuse her anything, and tonight she’ll beg him to open it.

briefs.title: The Hen House
briefs.objective: Leave without the police, and in a pair of borrowed trousers if he can manage it.
briefs.obstacle: No story explains the feathers, the old man won’t stop asking, and Felix has a terrible feeling he knows exactly where the hens went.

briefs.title: The Well At Cutbank
briefs.objective: Keep her well from being drained dry by the herd.
briefs.obstacle: He’s honest, his cattle are dying, and she knows what thirst looks like.

briefs.title: The Hammer Spring
briefs.objective: Keep him off the street at sundown without shaming him in front of the town.
briefs.obstacle: He’ll go out with a broken gun if he has to, the whole town heard him accept, and the honest answer to his question is yes, it can be fixed.

demands.belongsTo: Foreign-detective roles such as Poirot

briefs.title: The Cloakroom Ticket
briefs.objective: Make him listen to her solution.
briefs.obstacle: He isn’t interested, and halfway through she realizes the coat that solves it hangs on his own shoulders.

briefs.title: The Note Under The Storm
briefs.objective: Name the killer so clearly that no one in the room, or listening at home, can doubt it.
briefs.obstacle: Her evidence is only what she heard, the family thinks of her as hired help, and one of them has just told her to go back to her tuning fork.

briefs.title: The Teahouse Oath
briefs.objective: Keep her oath and keep her brother.
briefs.obstacle: He draws on her to force the issue, and she won’t draw her sword against him.

briefs.title: Learned Through The Shutters
briefs.objective: Be taken on as her student before she leaves the yard.
briefs.obstacle: The swordswoman barely answers her, the forms Anran copied are full of mistakes she can’t see, and her father needs her at the inn.

demands.belongsTo: ninkyo eiga (1960s chivalry yakuza films), the lead's climactic sword fight

briefs.title: The Last Lesson
briefs.objective: Get Daiki’s promise to quit the family and run the noodle shop straight.
briefs.obstacle: Daiki joined to earn his father’s respect, and quitting now would feel like losing to him.

briefs.title: Five Years From The Day
briefs.objective: Leave with an account, or at least with a date he can come back.
briefs.obstacle: The rule is clear, she can’t bend it, and his pride is the only thing he brought that won’t fit in the folder.

demands.belongsTo: the performers playing the undead

briefs.title: The Last Stop
briefs.objective: Find any way to keep him on the bus.
briefs.obstacle: There isn’t one, he knows it, and the children are twenty feet behind them.

briefs.title: The Left Sleeve
briefs.objective: Find out the truth about his arm before the ferry leaves.
briefs.obstacle: He swears it’s a dog bite from last week, she can’t prove otherwise from across a table, and his daughter is watching from the ferry’s rail.
